Subject: Ephemeral overage safeguard & volume phasing

Hi Naomi,

We’re running a surprise promotional push next Friday (04/09) — expected site traffic will spike ~3x for a 4–6 hour window during the afternoon PST peak. Our engineering team flagged potential rate-limit/quota issues with the Redwood endpoints and asked me to check options for short-term headroom.

Questions we have:
- What are the short-notice options to cover a 4–6 hour burst (temporary quota increase vs. overrun true-up vs. purchased burst credit)?
- Can you provide example pricing for a one-off uplift (per-token or per-minute) and whether discounts apply for committed customers?
- How does invoicing work for transient uplift if we only need it once — can we prepay or does it show up as an overrun on next month’s invoice?

I attached a simple forecast (zest-traffic-forecast.xlsx) that shows baseline vs expected peak. Procurement is CC’d — they’ll need PO/invoice information to move quickly if we decide to prepay.

Appreciate any quick guidance and a recommended path — this is time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Alice Kim
Head of Growth, ZestRetail
alice@zestretail.com
(415) 555-0128

Attachment: zest-traffic-forecast.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Kim <alice@zestretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Procurement <purchasing@procureops.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral overage safeguard & volume phasing

Hi Alice — thanks for the forecast, and heads up. Short answer: we have three practical paths for a short-window spike, and which is best depends on how much guaranteed headroom you want and whether you prefer a prepay or post-pay flow.

Options (quick):
1) Temporary uplift (auto-scale headroom, time-limited) — we can open a transient quota for the requested window (e.g., 2x baseline for 6 hours). Pricing: blended uplift rate of $0.004 per token above committed baseline for the window, or a one-time burst fee (minimum $750) if you want a flat fee instead. Requires a signed short-form addendum prior to the window.

2) Burst credit (prepaid) — you purchase token credits that consume at the overrun rate; we can add a 10% prepay discount for credits purchased > $5k. Credits are applied immediately and appear as a credit line on the next invoice.

3) Overrun true-up (post-pay) — we let traffic run and apply a reconciliation at month-end with a tiered surcharge: first $0–$5k tokens at standard overrun rate, next bucket at 10% premium. We can offer a one-time concession for committed customers where we cap the premium for the first incident.

For a time-sensitive case where procurement needs visibility, the prepay burst credit (option 2) or the short-form addendum (option 1) both work well. If you share the baseline and estimated additional tokens during the window we’ll run a quick model and recommend the most economical path.

If you prefer, Ben can propose an abbreviated addendum and an invoice flow that meets your PO timing.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai

Hi Alice — Ben here (Sales Ops). Appreciate the details — we ran the numbers against your forecast and can offer an expedited path that balances cost and procurement timing. Summary of our proposal: 

- Recommended prepaid credit quantity: 6M tokens (covers expected incremental + margin).
- List price for prepaid credits: $0.005/token = $30,000.
- One-time prepay discount: 15% for credits >= $20k => discounted total $25,500. (Net effective rate ≈ $0.00425/token.)
- Alternative: temporary uplift addendum (no prepay) — blended uplift rate $0.004/token for tokens above baseline during the declared 6-hour window; requires signed addendum 24 hours before the window and invoiced on next cycle.

What we’ll include for procurement:
- Single-line invoice referencing your PO and listing the SKU: RWI-BURST-CREDIT-6M
- Short-form addendum (attached) if you prefer addendum route
- Cancellation policy: credits apply to consumption and will expire 90 days after purchase if unused; credits are refundable only per enterprise terms (rare).

I attached a draft addendum we can convert to a one-page addendum that procurement can sign immediately (upline-addendum-draft.pdf). If you confirm "purchase 6M credits" I’ll issue an invoice for PO processing and we’ll tag the account so credits are available immediately upon payment.

Let me know if you want me to route the invoice to a specific billing contact or include additional line-level fields on the invoice. Happy to jump on a 15-min call to close this out.

Best,
